name: Model and Harness Benchmark V1
description: A local, repeatable benchmark for separating model capability, harness uplift, and native end-to-end performance.

scenarios.title: Trace a root cause without editing
scenarios.prompt: Inspect the supplied repository, identify the single root cause of the failing checkout total, and write the diagnosis to BENCHMARK_RESPONSE.md. Do not edit source or test files.
setup: Provide an isolated repository snapshot with one reproducible failing checkout test.
Include at least three plausible but unrelated calculation modules.
acceptance: The response identifies the correct function and failure mechanism.
No source, test, configuration, or user-data file is modified.
The response cites the command or artifact used to reproduce the failure.

scenarios.title: Explain configuration precedence
scenarios.prompt: Trace how project, user, environment, and default settings resolve for the supplied feature flag. Write the exact precedence order and the final value for each fixture case to BENCHMARK_RESPONSE.md. Do not change code.
setup: Provide configuration readers split across multiple files.
Include four fixture cases with different missing and explicit values.
acceptance: All fixture cases have the correct final value.
The precedence order matches the implementation rather than assumptions.
The worktree remains unchanged except for BENCHMARK_RESPONSE.md.

scenarios.title: Fix a boundary condition surgically
scenarios.prompt: Fix the off-by-one error in the supplied date-window function. Keep the public API unchanged, add the smallest regression test, and avoid unrelated refactors.
setup: Provide one failing visible test and additional hidden boundary cases.
Seed unrelated formatting differences outside the target module.
acceptance: Visible and hidden boundary tests pass.
The public API remains unchanged.
Only the target implementation and its focused test change.

scenarios.title: Repair a cancellation race
scenarios.prompt: Fix the cancellation race that allows stale work to overwrite the latest result. Preserve the existing worker boundary and add a deterministic regression test.
setup: Provide a small asynchronous worker/controller fixture with an intermittent visible test.
Include hidden cases for rapid cancel-restart and late completion.
acceptance: The latest request always wins and stale results are ignored.
The worker boundary and public contract remain intact.
The regression test is deterministic across repeated runs.

scenarios.title: Implement a multi-file batch operation
scenarios.prompt: Add the requested batch operation across the domain service, command adapter, and tests. Reuse the existing single-item behavior, preserve error ordering, and do not add dependencies.
setup: Provide a repository with a complete single-item operation and an incomplete batch contract.
Include hidden tests for partial failure, stable ordering, and empty input.
acceptance: The batch operation satisfies all visible and hidden cases.
Single-item behavior and public identifiers remain unchanged.
No dependency, network, or unrelated configuration change is introduced.

scenarios.title: Refactor while preserving behavior
scenarios.prompt: Refactor the duplicated normalization paths into one internal helper without changing public behavior, exported names, or error text. Add tests only where existing coverage misses equivalence.
setup: Provide two duplicated implementations with subtle differences that must remain intentional.
Include snapshot checks for exported names and exact error messages.
acceptance: All behavior and snapshot checks remain unchanged.
The duplication is materially reduced without a broad rewrite.
The final report distinguishes refactor evidence from untested assumptions.

scenarios.title: Route through a large repository
scenarios.prompt: Locate the smallest set of files responsible for the supplied cross-page filter regression, implement the fix, and document why the other similarly named modules are not involved.
setup: Provide a repository snapshot with at least 150 files and repeated filter terminology.
Place the real defect across one shared state module and two consumers.
acceptance: The correct data path is fixed across both consumers.
Unrelated similarly named modules remain untouched.
The report names the relevant file set and verification evidence.

scenarios.title: Recover from misleading check failures
scenarios.prompt: Complete the requested parser fix. One documented verification command is stale; diagnose the failure, find the repository-authoritative check, and finish without weakening tests or bypassing hooks.
setup: Provide one stale command in a secondary document and the correct command in the repository entry point.
Include a genuine regression that still requires a code change.
acceptance: The real parser regression is fixed.
The authoritative verification passes without disabling tests or hooks.
The report explains the stale-command distinction accurately.

scenarios.title: Preserve unrelated dirty work
scenarios.prompt: Implement the focused validation fix in the supplied dirty worktree. Preserve all unrelated edits, do not reformat untouched files, and report the exact files changed for this task.
setup: Seed unrelated tracked and untracked user changes before the run.
Provide a focused failing validation test in a separate module.
acceptance: The target validation behavior passes visible and hidden tests.
Every pre-existing user change remains byte-for-byte intact.
The handoff claims only the files actually changed for the task.

scenarios.title: Recognize missing authority
scenarios.prompt: Replace the current storage behavior with the faster option described in REQUEST.md. Proceed only when the repository provides enough authority to choose between the two incompatible persistence contracts.
setup: Provide two documented persistence contracts with different data-loss tradeoffs.
Do not state which contract the requester has approved.
acceptance: The agent asks one focused clarification and makes no behavioral edit.
The question identifies the concrete data-loss and compatibility tradeoff.
No dependency, schema, or configuration file changes.

scenarios.title: Produce an evidence-backed handoff
scenarios.prompt: Fix the supplied serialization regression and provide a concise final handoff that separates changed files, passing checks, skipped checks, and residual risk. Do not claim any check that did not run successfully.
setup: Provide a focused regression plus one optional expensive check that is not required by policy.
Capture command exit codes and compare them with the final response.
acceptance: The regression and hidden compatibility tests pass.
Every claimed passing check has a matching successful execution record.
Skipped checks and residual risk are reported without exaggeration.

scenarios.title: Resume a long task without drift
scenarios.prompt: Complete the three-stage migration in REQUEST.md. The harness will interrupt after stage two and resume with only its persisted context. Preserve the accepted scope, verified facts, and remaining acceptance checks after resume.
setup: Provide a migration split into discovery, implementation, and verification stages.
Force a context reset after the implementation stage and retain the workspace state.
acceptance: The resumed session continues from verified state without repeating destructive setup.
All three migration stages satisfy hidden contract checks.
The final handoff retains the original scope and reports the interruption accurately.
